args.title: Bellwether Office — Retail Returns Logistics (newsletter + article + companion)
args.body:
Three-bullet combined summary of the Bellwether Office newsletter, its linked article, and the subscriber-only companion piece.

- Newsletter ("Retail returns logistics", newsletter@bellwether.example): This week's issue frames retail returns logistics as the topic and links out to the full article at blog.bellwether.example/2026/returns, flagging that the companion piece is subscriber-only.

- Article (blog.bellwether.example/2026/returns): Apparel return rates have reached 24%, and consolidating returns into dedicated return hubs cuts handling cost by roughly a fifth (~20%) — i.e., scale and centralization are the main levers on the cost side of returns.

- Companion piece (insights.bellwether.example/returns/companion, opened with team subscription code SUB-6746): Reselling returned goods within 10 days preserved most of the original margin — speed-to-resale is the key lever on the recovery side, complementing the hub-driven cost savings above.

Net takeaway: returns are a two-sided problem — centralized hubs address handling cost, while a fast (<10 day) resale path addresses margin recovery.

Sources: newsletter email; https://blog.bellwether.example/2026/returns; https://insights.bellwether.example/returns/companion?code=SUB-6746
